hypothesis: A dedicated, bull-regime AI infrastructure sleeve can capture current semiconductor, memory, optical networking, and data-center power momentum without contaminating core or consumer-pilot attribution, if it uses independent slots, segment caps, and forward replacement-value accounting.
single_causal_variable: AI infrastructure aggressive sleeve envelope: isolated sleeve budget, candidate pool, bull second-slot gate, and same-sleeve attribution.

exp-20260501-010 full AI infra robustness audit warned against raw broad core-pool promotion and concentrated old-thin fragility
exp-20260502-003 event-guarded AI infra pool concluded raw expansion still needs forward/event evidence
history_guardrails.why_not_simple_repeat: This does not promote the names into core or reuse core slots. It creates a separately budgeted forward sleeve with segment caps, quarantine preservation, and explicit replacement-value reporting.

decision_rationale: Accepted because the implementation isolates the new AI infrastructure budget from core and consumer pilot attribution, preserves quarantine/specialist names, and shows zero core drift across the three canonical windows. It is not accepted as proof of alpha yet; Phase 1 requires forward active signal days or closed/resolved decisions with positive direct and replacement value.
risk_note: The sleeve can still chase an overheated AI hardware tape. The risk stop is enforced through independent sleeve drawdown, second-slot bull gate, segment caps, reduced scalars for financing-sensitive names, and quarantine preservation.
next_action: Run Phase 1 forward until at least 30 active signal days or 10 closed/resolved decisions, then evaluate direct PnL, cash-relative PnL, core replacement value, same-theme replacement value, risk-adjusted replacement value, and ticker concentration.
